transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I just don’t care about any of the things I used to love doing anymore—not fishing, not cooking, not even singing at church. Ever since my wife passed away, I just can't find it in me to do any of it.
How long have you been feeling this way since your wife passed away, and did these symptoms start right after her death or after a delay?

My wife passed away about a year and a half ago, and though I tried to keep busy at first, everything caught up to me pretty quickly. This heavy depression has been with me steadily for a little over a year now, and those unsettling feelings of being watched started about a year and a month ago.
Have you had most days with low mood or loss of interest for at least two weeks in a row, or has it been more of a stress reaction that comes and goes with the loss of your wife?

No, it doesn't really come and go at all. This heavy, empty depression has been with me almost every single day, from morning to night, for a little over a year now. I can only think of a few scattered days during this whole time when I didn't feel completely weighed down.
Have you had any unusual experiences like hearing voices, seeing things others do not, or feeling strongly that someone is watching or trying to harm you?

I don't hear voices or see things, but I do strongly feel like I'm being watched and targeted. I'm convinced that some folks from my church and the hospital where my wife died are keeping tabs on me to punish me, taking things like the late mail or a flickering TV as messages. My sisters tell me it's crazy talk, but it feels very real to me.
Have you ever felt so depressed that you thought life was not worth living, or had thoughts of harming yourself?

Yes, more nights than I'd like to admit, I lie in bed thinking it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. I've even caught myself picturing taking all my blood pressure pills at once, though I haven't actually gone through with it. It just feels like too much to carry sometimes.
When you feel watched or targeted, do you ever worry that these beliefs might not be true, or are you completely certain they are real?

Even though my sisters tell me it's just crazy talk, when the mail is late or the TV flickers, it feels completely real to me. I feel certain they are keeping tabs on me and trying to punish me, and it is just really hard to shake that feeling.
Have you ever had times when the suspicious beliefs happened even when your depression was not present, or do they only occur when you feel very depressed?

Yes, there was actually a stretch late last summer when I wasn't feeling quite as tearful or deeply depressed. But even during those weeks, I was still completely convinced that the people from the church and the hospital were tracking me and sending me signs. It seemed like that feeling of being watched just kept going, even when the heavy sadness lifted a bit.
Have you ever had the suspicious beliefs or feeling that people were watching or targeting you even when you were not depressed at all, or do they only happen during your depressive episodes?

Yes, during that stretch late last summer, I wasn't feeling depressed or tearful at all, but those feelings of being watched didn't go away. I was still absolutely convinced that the people from my church and the hospital were tracking me and sending me signs, even without the heavy sadness.
Have you ever had the feeling that people were watching or targeting you even during times when you were not depressed at all, or did those beliefs only happen when your depression was present?

Yes, like I said, last summer there was a stretch of a few weeks where the heavy sadness lifted and I wasn't tearful at all. But even during that time, I was still absolutely convinced that the church and hospital folks were tracking me and sending me signs through the TV and mail.

Have you ever had periods of at least a month when you were not depressed but still had these beliefs that people were watching or targeting you, or did the beliefs always happen only when you were depressed?

Yes, late last summer there was a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't feeling depressed at all, though I don't think it was quite a whole month. Even during those weeks when the dark mood was gone, I still strongly believed that the church and hospital folks were tracking me and sending me signs.
Have there ever been periods of at least a month when you were not depressed at all but still strongly believed people were watching or targeting you?

No, I don't think it has ever been a whole month like that. Late last summer was the longest stretch, but that was only about two or three weeks where the depression lifted while I still felt watched.
Have you ever had a full month or longer when you were not depressed at all but still strongly believed people were watching or targeting you?

No, I've never had a full month like that. It's really just been that two or three-week period last summer where the sadness went away but the tracking didn't. Most of the time, the heavy depression and the feeling of being watched have been there together.
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or felt like your thoughts were racing?

No, I’ve never had any times like that with high energy or racing thoughts. It’s actually been the complete opposite for me—I just feel constantly weighed down, empty, and extremely slowed down, like I'm moving through molasses.
Have you ever had a full month or longer when you were not depressed at all but still strongly believed people were watching or targeting you?

Thinking back, I suppose that stretch late last summer actually did last for about a month or so when the heavy depression lifted a bit and I wasn't as tearful. But even during that whole time, I was still absolutely certain that the people from the church and the hospital were tracking me and sending me signs.

During that month when you were not feeling depressed, did the belief that people were watching or targeting you continue even though your mood was normal, or did it only happen when you were depressed?

Yes, they definitely continued even though my mood had lifted. Even without the heavy sadness, I was still completely convinced that the church and hospital folks were tracking me and sending me signs. It was like that feeling of being watched just wouldn't let up, no matter how my mood was.
Have you ever had at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed at all but still had these beliefs that people were watching or targeting you?

Yes, that stretch late last summer lasted for about a month, so it was definitely longer than two weeks. Even though the heavy depression and tearfulness had cleared up during that time, I was still completely convinced they were tracking me and sending me signs.
Have you ever had a time of at least two weeks when you were not depressed at all, but you still had these beliefs that people were watching or targeting you?

Yes, that stretch late last summer was definitely at least a month long, so it was well over two weeks. Even though the heavy depression and tearfulness had cleared up during those weeks, I was still completely convinced they were tracking me and sending me signs.
Have you ever had hallucinations, disorganized speech, or very disorganized behavior, or has it mainly been the fixed belief that people are watching or targeting you?

I don't hear or see things, but I definitely struggle with my speech and behavior alongside feeling watched. When I try to talk, my mind jumps all over the place—like going from choir practice to the Bahamas in one breath—and some days I just freeze in place or pace around muttering prayers. Those beliefs about being watched and targeted are also very much there and feel completely real.

Have you ever had a time of at least 2 weeks when you had no depression at all, but you still had the disorganized speech or odd behavior along with the belief that people were watching or targeting you?

Yes, during that stretch late last summer when the depression lifted for about a month, those other things didn't go away either. Even though I wasn't feeling sad, my mind was still jumping all over the place when I tried to talk, and I would still freeze up or pace around muttering prayers while feeling watched. It was like all of those thoughts and behaviors kept going right along with the feeling that I was being tracked.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports schizoaffective disorder: the patient has a major depressive syndrome with persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, psychomotor slowing, and suicidal ideation, plus clear psychotic symptoms (persecutory delusions) and disorganized speech/behavior. Critically, there was at least a month-long period where psychotic symptoms and disorganization persisted despite the absence of depressive symptoms, satisfying the requirement for psychosis outside mood episodes.
